key_insight: A projectability-guided atomic-orbital construction lets deep-learning Hamiltonian models learn compact, accurate targets from plane-wave DFT, including hybrid-functional nonlocal effects.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more transferable electronic-structure prediction by bridging plane-wave reference calculations with equivariant neural Hamiltonian learning.
method: Select high-projectability plane-wave eigenstates to define the retained AO subspace.
Add selected higher-energy states to complete the basis without an empirical energy shift.
Build PBE/HSE AO Hamiltonians from PW eigenvalues/eigenstates, preserving nonlocal contributions implicitly.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on MoS2 and sodium phases show the constructed AO Hamiltonians reproduce plane-wave band structures accurately with smaller bases than real-space reconstruction.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful state selection and projectability thresholds, which may affect robustness across more complex materials systems.
paper_title: Accurately Generalizing Deep-Learning Hamiltonian Methods to Plane-Wave Density Functional Theory
